title: China’s hottest stocks these days have one thing in common: names that sound like sheep
html:
Shares of fish processors, lighting manufacturers and appliance makers have soared ahead of the Year of the Sheep. Investor appetite has had little to do with the status of their businesses.

On Nov. 3, shares of Septwolves, a Chinese menswear company, jumped 10% — the maximum allowed in a single day — for the second straight session. Business wasn’t suddenly booming. Traders had simply discovered a new reason to buy the stock CN:002029: Wolves eat sheep.

And, with the Year of the Sheep approaching, sheep were suddenly a big deal in China’s stock market.
summary: Shares of fish processors, lighting manufacturers and appliance makers have soared ahead of the Year of the Sheep. Investor appetite has had little to do with the status of their businesses.
